chapter: Harlem, Redman's band and the Savoy
title: Seventh Avenue as a boulevard
summary: Seventh Avenue was a beautiful promenade, immaculately dressed and peaceful, while rougher people lived near Park Avenue.

blocks.x: : What was Seventh Avenue like, right around that corner?

A beautiful street. Seventh Avenue was a beautiful street. The people that walked on Seventh Avenue in those days were beautiful. You never seen a man or woman walk down Seventh Avenue in those days unless he was immaculately dressed.
: It was a promenade. It was a boulevard.

It was. It was a boulevard. Beautiful flowers in the middle, you know. And everybody would come out in the afternoon, they would come out to meet your friends, you know. And it was just a beautiful place, and people were beautiful. There was no hassles, no hassles. You didn't -- no hassles.
The bad people lived over on Park Avenue along the railroad tracks, the New York Central, over that way, --
